races.name: Slater Menswear Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ginger Mail
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose 10-year-old legs may struggle to cope with the expected strong pace despite his experience
runners_data.comment: Exposed 10yo whose powers would appear to be on the wane
runners_data.spotlight: Exposed 10yo whose powers would appear to be on the wane judged on this season's performances; opposable.

runners_data.name: Triple Crown Ted
runners_data.note: Natural leader who beat Bertie's Ballet at Kelso and was confidently handled when second here last time
runners_data.comment: Confidently ridden when second here last time; looks capable of better again
runners_data.spotlight: Beat Lance Les Des and Bertie's Ballet off 4lb lower at Kelso in February (2m, heavy) and he was confidently ridden out the back when second over C&D last time (soft), where a late mistake didn't help; strong suspicion that he more to offer and the yard, also represented by Caballo De Guerra, won this with a novice two years ago.

runners_data.name: Bibe Mus
runners_data.note: Paul Nicholls hold-up horse who won his stable debut comfortably and should relish the expected strong gallop
runners_data.comment: Debut winner for this yard and his Fred Winter run was better that it looks on paper
runners_data.spotlight: 1m2f French Flat winner who did well for former Irish connections, in victory and defeat over hurdles; even better when winning comfortably on his stable debut at Sandown (soft) and it was only three days later he finished well held under a penalty (same mark here) in the Fred Winter, though that run was better than it looks on paper; this is his first handicap against older opposition and he's very much in the mix.

runners_data.name: Ravenscraig Castle
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with just one hurdles win in 17 attempts, exposed and outclassed at this level
runners_data.comment: Consistent but not progressive; fifth in this last year off the very same mark
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success in 17 runs over hurdles came at Perth last summer (2m, good); he's consistent but not progressive and was a well-held fifth in this last year off the very same mark.

runners_data.name: The Gray Ghost
runners_data.note: Versatile prominent runner who has been consistent across varying trips but faces a tough task off this high mark
runners_data.comment: In form but does look vulnerable off this high a mark in this strong a race
runners_data.spotlight: Versatile trip-wise as his recent run of solid form has been from 1m7f to 3m; should give his running but does look vulnerable off this high a mark in this strong a race.

runners_data.name: Secret Force
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 76 days off but has class having won at this level before for Cromwell
runners_data.comment: Highly tried since winning his 3yo hurdle; new headgear for this handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: On his first two runs for this yard he won a 1m3f handicap on heavy and a 3yo hurdle on good to yielding; not so good since, albeit at Grade 2 and Listed level; might yet do better again and canny Irish trainer fits two new forms of headgear for this handicap debut; interesting.

runners_data.name: Lance Les Des
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from the Alexander stable who has been consistent this season and suits the expected pace scenario

runners_data.name: Bertie's Ballet
runners_data.note: Front-runner who won off this mark at Haydock last season but has struggled to recapture that form recently
runners_data.comment: Below par in two of his three races this season but he's on his last winning mark
runners_data.spotlight: Won a Class 3 handicap at Haydock last season off this mark so wouldn't be too dismissive about his chances despite failing to reach anything like the same level in two of his three races this campaign.

runners_data.name: Newtown Rambler
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader making just his second start for Keatley in new headgear after Irish point success
runners_data.comment: Made all at Warwick; it's tougher dominating around here and he's 6lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden winner in Ireland and later placed in handicaps over fences; only his second run for this yard when dropped back to 2m in this new headgear combination at Warwick (good to soft) and he made pretty much every yard; it will be tougher dominating this stronger field on this more galloping track, and he's 6lb higher.

runners_data.name: Dance Thief
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose three career wins have all been at this venue but others are preferred
runners_data.comment: Over fences for his last three races and has been good and bad; others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: All three wins have been here, a hurdle and two chases; over fences for his last three races and has been good and bad; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Magna Victor
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced prominent horse who is 2-2 in handicaps but faces an 8lb rise for his Musselburgh success
runners_data.comment: Up 8lb for winning a weaker race last time but he does seem on an upward curve
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 7yo who is 2-2 since sent into handicaps, both wins over 1m7f on good to soft ground at Musselburgh; an 8lb rise seems harsh enough for last time, for all that he won readily, and this a lot deeper; still respected with him on an upward curve.

runners_data.name: Caballo De Guerra
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who races too freely but has the class to be competitive if settling better in new headgear
runners_data.comment: Raced too freely in a Grade 2 last time; the ability is there should the hood help
runners_data.spotlight: Kelso novice winner in October (2m, good; effective on soft) and continued to run well until racing too freely in a Grade 2 at Kelso last time out; well held in a bumper when he tried a hood once before but this aid is worth another go.

runners_data.name: Castle Ivers
runners_data.note: Natural leader returning from 512 days off but showed high-class form when winning at Warwick in November
runners_data.comment: Has a long absence to overcome and a hefty weight for his handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Point and dual bumper winner who was a shade of odds-on when leading late on in a big-field maiden at Warwick in November 2024 (good to soft; won on soft); has a long absence to overcome and a hefty weight for his handicap debut, but trainer has spoken well of him.

runners_data.name: Belaya River
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who gets significant weight relief but disappointed badly when switched to handicaps at Sedgefield
runners_data.comment: Returning to slower ground may help but unlikely that he's on that great a mark
runners_data.spotlight: Flat background; mildly progressive when first then second in two 4yo hurdles but he ran miserably switched to handicaps at Sedgefield where his jumping didn't stand the test; returning to slower ground may help but unlikely that he's on that great a mark.

runners_data.name: Tuppence
runners_data.note: Prominent maiden who took too strong a hold on handicap debut but benefits from the 7lb claiming allowance
runners_data.comment: Dropping back to 2m could work but this still commands a career best and by some way
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced maiden who took too strong a hold when a fading fourth on handicap debut at Musselburgh four weeks ago (good to soft); dropping back to 2m from 2m4f could work but this still commands a career best and by some way.

races.paceDynamic: Castle Ivers, Triple Crown Ted, Bertie's Ballet and Newtown Rambler will ensure a strong gallop from the start, with at least three of these confirmed front-runners likely to dispute the early lead. The pace will be testing throughout on this soft ground over 2 miles, creating a stamina examination that will sort out the field. The strong early gallop will stretch the field and expose any that lack genuine staying power. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and prominent racers with proven stamina, as the pace-setters will likely weaken in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace-setters go too fast early and collapse in the final half-mile
scenarios.body: The strong gallop will set up perfectly for horses ridden with restraint who can stay the trip strongly. Late-running types like Bibe Mus, Secret Force and Caballo De Guerra will have their chance to sweep up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the handy horses can sit just off the pace and time their challenge
scenarios.body: A horse like The Gray Ghost or Magna Victor tracking the leaders could find the perfect position to strike when the front-runners weaken. Their tactical speed from a prominent position will prove decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one pace-setter proves stronger than the others and maintains galloping room
scenarios.body: Castle Ivers or Triple Crown Ted could dictate terms and prove too tough to peg back if getting first run on their rivals. Their class and tactical advantage from the front will be hard to overcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightweight Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too strong for the big weights and a lightly-weighted runner stays on
scenarios.body: Belaya River or Tuppence could benefit from their weight advantage if the gallop becomes punishing enough to stop the market leaders. The handicapper's assistance combined with stamina will prove telling.

watchPoints.text: Castle Ivers returning from 512 days absence - fitness levels unknown despite his class advantage
Bertie's Ballet and Newtown Rambler both likely to contest the early lead which could compromise both their chances
Triple Crown Ted was confidently handled when second here last time suggesting connections expected more to come
Bibe Mus returning from 38 days off for Paul Nicholls who is operating at 18% strike-rate with his runners
Secret Force and Caballo De Guerra both wear headgear changes which could aid their settling and tactical positioning

races.name: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Risk De Pluie
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose recent Chepstow win shows improved chase form, with Sam Twiston-Davies a positive jockey booking and the soft ground suiting perfectly
runners_data.comment: In good form at Chepstow on last two starts; optimism he'll be fine back down in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten on first seven chase starts but showed improved form to win comfortably at Chepstow (2m3f, soft) in February and he bumped into a progressive winner there (2m3f, soft) last month, when clear of the third; there can be optimism that he will be fine back down in trip and he's respected.

runners_data.name: Throatlash
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner returning from a fall but with perfect 3-3 chase record beforehand, must jump cleaner than at Haydock to utilize his early speed
runners_data.comment: Front-runner; under pressure when falling last time but 3-3 in handicap chases previously
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner; made mistakes and was under pressure when falling three out at Haydock (2m4f, soft) two months ago; however, he was 3-3 in handicap chases (1m7f-2m4f, soft/good to soft) previously and this very lightly raced 7yo may still have more to offer.

runners_data.name: The Grafter
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with excellent recent Newcastle form, though the step up to 2m½f may stretch his stamina on testing ground
runners_data.comment: 2-2 over fences and something to spare each time; may well have more left in the tank
runners_data.spotlight: Built upon his hurdling promise to win on chase/seasonal debut at Newcastle (2m, heavy) in January and he followed up there (2m, good to soft) in February; climbing the weights but this unexposed 7yo had something to spare for both wins and may well have more left in the tank.

runners_data.name: Ballyfort
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse well suited by the course and distance combination, with solid recent form over C&D giving him a clear fitness advantage
runners_data.comment: Likes it here & has won twice this term but needs to be better than ever back up in grade
runners_data.spotlight: Made it two wins for the season when scoring over C&D (soft) in January and bounced back from lesser run here when 1l second of five over C&D (soft) last month; could give another good account but he needs to be better than ever back up in grade if he's to win today.

runners_data.name: Pleasington
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner whose chase form suggests he's well handicapped, though the fall last time and 48-day break raise fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: He's struggled on his last two runs but perhaps wind op/cheekpieces will make a difference
runners_data.spotlight: Two-time novice hurdle winner who ran well in defeat this term on two of his first three chase starts (1m7f/2m, soft/good) and is on a handy mark on that form; he's struggled on his last two runs and has something to prove but perhaps the wind op and first-time cheekpieces will make a difference.

runners_data.name: Koukeo
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose early season chase form was excellent, but recent Newbury disappointments suggest confidence may be fragile under pressure
runners_data.comment: Disappointing on last 2 runs but good start to chasing career previously; may bounce back
runners_data.spotlight: Won his first two chase starts in January (2m, good/good to soft) under Jonjo O'Neill, who is back on board today; disappointing at Newbury on his last two outings but the first was a tough assignment over 2m4f and he jumped badly last time; it wouldn't be a surprise to see him bounce back.

runners_data.name: Marty McFly
runners_data.note: Progressive prominent runner in excellent form with four wins from four this year, though the 7lb rise and step up in class pose serious questions
runners_data.comment: Arrives on a five-timer and latest 7lb rise may not stop this thriving 8yo
runners_data.spotlight: Prominent racer who made it 4-4 for 2026 (1m7f-2m4f, good to soft/good) at Carlisle last month; won by 3l last time and a 7lb rise may not stop this thriving 8yo, provided the forecast soft ground isn't an issue.

runners_data.name: Stuntman Steve
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose poor recent chase form makes him hard to fancy despite being theoretically well handicapped on old hurdle form
runners_data.comment: Hard to fancy on chasing evidence but this Irish raider is well treated on his hurdle form
runners_data.spotlight: Hard to fancy on the evidence of his four runs over fences this year; however, he's well handicapped on last summer's hurdle form and he's from a respected Irish stable; one to watch in the betting.

runners_data.name: Tanking Along
runners_data.note: Front-runner whose left-handed course preference and cheekpieces combination could provide the tactical edge needed to exploit his light weight
runners_data.comment: Two wins at Sedgefield this season but 8lb wrong today and the cheekpieces are left off
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive in cheekpieces, winning at Sedgefield in November (2m1f, soft; hurdles) and March (2m, good; fences); should appreciate going back left-handed after being soundly beaten at Carlisle last time but he's 8lb out of the handicap today and the cheekpieces are left off.

races.paceDynamic: Throatlash and Tanking Along will contest the early lead, with both horses natural front-runners who need to dictate terms. Throatlash's aggressive style and Tanking Along's progressive form suggest they'll set a solid gallop from the off. The soft ground and 2m½f trip will test stamina reserves, likely creating a searching pace that could crack some rivals before the home turn. This honest tempo strongly favours prominent racers and hold-up horses with proven stamina, as pure speed horses will struggle to sustain their effort in the testing conditions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Throatlash Dominates Early
scenarios.trigger: If Throatlash jumps cleanly and avoids the mistakes that caused his Haydock fall
scenarios.body: His front-running style will capitalize on the soft ground that suits him perfectly, and weaker stayers will be cooked by halfway. The honest gallop plays directly into the hands of proven stayers like The Grafter and Risk De Pluie who can pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Competitive Pace Battle
scenarios.trigger: If both Throatlash and Tanking Along go hard early and compromise each other
scenarios.body: The dual pace angle creates a strong gallop that sets up the race perfectly for hold-up horses with tactical speed. Pleasington and Ballyfort can use their class and finishing kick to sweep past tiring leaders in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tanking Along Takes Charge
scenarios.trigger: If Throatlash makes early errors or is restrained, leaving Tanking Along alone in front
scenarios.body: The progressive 7-year-old can utilize his improved jumping and left-handed course preference to control the race from the front. His modest rating means the weight relief combined with the tactical advantage could prove decisive against classier but less well-positioned rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners fall or make significant jumping errors early in the race
scenarios.body: The field will bunch up and create a sprint finish that doesn't suit most of these stamina-laden performers. Only horses with natural pace like Koukeo or Marty McFly can capitalize on the changed complexion, though the soft ground still demands stamina.

watchPoints.text: Throatlash must jump much cleaner than his Haydock fall suggests, as early mistakes will immediately compromise his front-running tactics
The pace battle between Throatlash and Tanking Along could become unsustainably fast and set up the race for back-markers with stamina
Marty McFly's four-race winning streak faces its biggest test with the 7lb penalty and significant class rise from previous targets
The Grafter's hold-up style needs the pace to be strong enough to bring stamina into play over this extended trip
Koukeo's confidence must be rebuilt after two disappointing runs when previously unbeaten over fences in his first two chase starts

races.name: Abbott Risk Consulting Ltd Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Green Angel
runners_data.note: Lone leader with sustainable style but needs to prove stamina after 66 days off and poor recent form over shorter trips.
runners_data.comment: 2m4f perhaps too far last time; previous Down Royal fourth over 2m1f was a good effort
runners_data.spotlight: A good run to be fourth on yielding ground in a 2m1f maiden at Down Royal in December and when below that level here two months ago he was sent over 2m4f (on soft); connections presumably not fazed by today's ground and, returned to shorter, he shouldn't be far away.

runners_data.name: Lirion
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with classy bumper form, perfectly positioned behind uncontested leader after 53-day break.
runners_data.comment: Two encouraging runs in bumpers, the latest after a long absence; hurdle debut
runners_data.spotlight: Bought for £60,000 after finishing an 11l second to the classy Mydaddypaddy in a Huntingdon bumper last March; only returned this February when beaten a short-head here by a Russell/Scudamore horse with potential; now goes over hurdles.

runners_data.name: Dropematthestation
runners_data.note: Strong prominent style with consistent maiden placings, wind surgery may unlock improvement in this tactical setup.
runners_data.comment: Has been weakening over longer trips in previous maidens; had a wind operation
runners_data.spotlight: Has been running well for a long way before weakening in maidens over 2m3f and 2m5f (tongue tied in final run); could have a better run in him after wind surgery and he's of definite interest.

runners_data.name: Linalene
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who ran his best race at this course and distance, but may need another step forward to win.
runners_data.comment: By some way it was his best performance yet when second to odds-on winner here last time
runners_data.spotlight: By some way it was his best performance yet when the only one to give the odds-on winner a race over C&D (soft) in late March; may need to take another step forward here but that's quite feasible.

runners_data.name: Bohemond Antioch
runners_data.note: Solid prominent performer returning from 112-day break, respectable hurdles form but yet to win in eight attempts.
runners_data.comment: Below par at Christmas but had a break and can go well if back on song
runners_data.spotlight: 0-3 in bumpers and 0-4 over hurdles, but has some respectable form and wasn't himself at Sedgefield last time when held at his point of departure; had a break since Christmas and can go well if back on song.

runners_data.name: Magna Patch
runners_data.note: Prominent style but minimal rules experience and heavy defeats suggest outclassed in this company.
runners_data.comment: Close second in point bumper but it's been a quiet start under rules
runners_data.spotlight: Close second in point bumper but it's been a quiet start under rules with 286 days separating heavy defeats in a bumper and novice hurdle.

runners_data.name: Penn Avenue
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with flat speed but poor recent hurdles form, benefits from 4-year-old weight allowance.
runners_data.comment: 0-6 over hurdles; gets all the allowances as a 4yo filly but others have greater upside
runners_data.spotlight: Dual Flat winner; 0-6 over hurdles and the worst of those runs was the latest in a handicap at Carlisle; gets all the allowances as a 4yo filly but others probably have greater upside even if she is back to something like her best.

runners_data.name: Culzean
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with no worthwhile form, can be dismissed based on consistent poor performances.
runners_data.comment: No worthwhile form in bumpers or over hurdles and she can be readily dismissed
runners_data.spotlight: No worthwhile form in bumpers or over hurdles and she can be readily dismissed.

races.paceDynamic: Green Angel will lead from the start with no other confirmed front runners to pressure him, creating a comfortable sustainable pace through the first mile. The prominent runners Lirion, Dropematthestation, Linalene, and Bohemond Antioch will track behind in a pack, while Penn Avenue and Culzean sit at the back as hold-up horses. With Green Angel allowed to dictate terms unchallenged, the race will develop into a tactical affair that strongly favours the prominent runners who can position just behind the leader and kick when ready. This race shape clearly benefits prominent runners who can travel well and have something left to finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Green Angel sets uncontested fractions and the prominent pack travels well.
scenarios.body: The pace-tracking horses get first run on the tiring leader turning for home, with the best of them having enough left to hold off any late challengers. Lirion and Dropematthestation are perfectly positioned to exploit this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Success
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes crawling and kicks late.
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get maximum benefit from a sprint finish where early position matters less than finishing kick. Penn Avenue's flat speed becomes crucial in a dash to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Green Angel gets soft early fractions and finds more when challenged.
scenarios.body: The leader uses his uncontested position to build an unassailable advantage, holding on despite late pressure. His recent course form at the distance gives him the edge in a staying battle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Green Angel stops quickly and the prominent pack comes back to the field.
scenarios.body: The entire complexion changes when the pace dissolves, creating a muddled finish where any horse can win. The best stayers benefit from the messy development.

watchPoints.text: Green Angel setting crawling fractions early - if he's not moving freely in the first half-mile he may not last home.
Lirion and Dropematthestation traveling strongly approaching two out - both have the tactical advantage to strike first.
Penn Avenue's position turning in - needs to be within striking distance to use her flat speed effectively.
Bohemond Antioch jumping fluently after his 112-day absence - any jumping errors will compromise his chances from prominent position.
The pace through the first mile - if Green Angel goes too fast early the race opens up for all horses behind him.

races.name: Hillhouse Quarry Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Califet En Vol
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who made costly mistakes at Kempton but has winning form over course and distance on soft ground
runners_data.comment: Won at Kempton in February and mistakes didn't help when soundly beaten there last time
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten fourth at Kempton (2m4f, good) last month but mistakes didn't help; won there (2m4f, good to soft) two starts ago and he can be in the mix if cutting out the errors; probably okay on soft ground.

runners_data.name: Twinjets
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner back in form with Jay Tidball, excellent soft ground record and two wins at this trip previously
runners_data.comment: Front-runner who was second at Newbury last month and can make another bold bid
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner; won two in a row last autumn (2m3f/2m4f, good to soft) and back to form when second under Jay Tidball at Newbury (2m4f, good to soft) last month; effective on soft earlier in career; can make another bold bid.

runners_data.name: Il Ridoto
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing tongue-tie and top-clip for the first time, suggesting connections expect improvement from Paul Nicholls stable

runners_data.name: Hoe Joly Smoke
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has had wind surgery since last run and showed his best form in third-place finishes recently
runners_data.comment: Has had wind surgery and top trainer has won five of the last eight runnings of this race
runners_data.spotlight: He hasn't quite been at the top of his game on his last two starts; however, he's had wind surgery since and is certainly of interest on his two third-place finishes at Cheltenham in the autumn (3m1f/2m4f, good/soft); top trainer has won five of the last eight runnings of this race.

runners_data.name: Donnacha
runners_data.note: Prominent runner prone to mistakes but has excellent soft ground form and won quality Cheltenham handicap in January after 83-day break
runners_data.comment: Won a quality handicap at Cheltenham in January and a 5lb rise isn't harsh
runners_data.spotlight: Can make mistakes but he was runner-up twice in a row prior to winning a quality handicap at Cheltenham (2m4f, soft) in January, when clear with subsequent Ultima runner-up Jagwar; a 5lb rise for that career-best performance isn't harsh and he's entitled to respect.

runners_data.name: Myretown
runners_data.note: Front-runner prone to bad blunders who arrives with something to prove after heavy defeats but retains promise on home track
runners_data.comment: Has something to prove but major player if tapping back into last season's promise
runners_data.spotlight: Prone to making a bad blunder and arrives with something to prove following heavy defeats on his last two starts; however, he hasn't been devoid of promise this season and he'll be a major player if tapping back into the promise shown when romping to victory at last season's Cheltenham Festival.

runners_data.name: Jipcot
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing tongue-tie who was well beaten at Cheltenham but made all to win comfortably at Leicester over longer trip
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Cheltenham last month but that may not be his track; in good heart before
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in the Plate last month but Cheltenham may not be his track; comfortably made all in small field at Leicester (2m6f, good to soft) in January and led into the straight at Ascot (3m, good to soft) in February, only to weaken; also effective on soft; could be involved.

runners_data.name: Dubai Days
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up performer wearing headband and tongue-tie who won over course and distance in February with excellent Ayr record
runners_data.comment: 11 visits to Ayr have yielded five wins and this is his time of year; could go well
runners_data.spotlight: Won over C&D (soft) in February before respectable sixth of 17 in veterans' final at Haydock (2m4f, good) a fortnight ago; 11 visits to Ayr have yielded five wins and this is his time of year; could go well.

runners_data.name: Hombre De Guerra
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing tongue-tie who hasn't been competitive this term but shaped as though needing this longer trip at Kelso
runners_data.comment: Yet to get competitive this season but his three wins have all come at Ayr
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't got competitive this term and beaten 18l when sixth of eight on stable debut at Kelso (2m1f, good to soft) in February; however, he shaped as though this step up in trip might be a good move and his three wins, including two over fences last January (2m, soft), have all come at Ayr.

races.paceDynamic: Twinjets and Myretown will ensure genuine pace from the start, with both confirmed front-runners likely to go forward and contest the early lead. This honest gallop over 2m4½f on soft ground will create a searching test of stamina, particularly through the closing stages where the pace will tell. The strong early pace will stretch the field and create opportunities for those with tactical speed to move through the race. This setup clearly favours prominent racers and hold-up horses who can finish strongly, as the early pace battle will soften up the leaders for late challengers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace between Twinjets and Myretown is genuinely strong and honest
scenarios.body: The soft ground and sustained gallop will find out the leaders in the final half-mile, allowing patient hold-up performers to close with late runs. Horses like Hoe Joly Smoke, Jipcot and Dubai Days can use their finishing kicks to maximum effect.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one horse can track the pace without getting embroiled in the early battle
scenarios.body: A prominent runner like Donnacha or Il Ridoto can position perfectly behind the leaders before striking with a well-timed challenge. They avoid the pace war but stay close enough to pounce when the leaders weaken.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Twinjets gets first run and kicks clear before Myretown can respond
scenarios.body: His class and recent form suggest he can dominate from the front if he gets an uncontested lead. The Paul Nicholls runner has won two in a row previously and showed he's back to form at Newbury.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too hard early and come back badly
scenarios.body: A moderate pace from tired leaders allows an unfancied hold-up horse to sneak through when others have used their ammunition. This chaotic finish suits the outsiders with something left in the tank.

watchPoints.text: Myretown is prone to making bad blunders and has been heavily defeated on his last two starts, making him unreliable despite home advantage
Both Twinjets and Myretown going forward together could set up a pace duel that compromises both front-runners if they get competitive early
Il Ridoto wears first-time tongue-tie and top-clip suggesting Paul Nicholls expects significant improvement from this prominent runner
Hoe Joly Smoke returns from wind surgery after 55 days off, which could either unlock improvement or indicate ongoing issues
Dubai Days has an excellent Ayr record with five wins from 11 visits and won over course and distance on soft ground in February

races.name: Coral Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: The Four Sixes
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 27 days off with questionable recent form over fences and hurdles
runners_data.comment: Easily made all in this last year but he's struggled for form since chase win in December
runners_data.spotlight: Easily made all in this last year when 5lb higher and he's one to watch in the betting; however, he's struggled for form over fences/hurdles since winning a novice chase at Kelso in December.

runners_data.name: Saracen Beau
runners_data.note: Hold-up merchant with excellent recent form and strong course record, ideally suited to strong pace

runners_data.name: Irandando Has
runners_data.comment: Two novice hurdle wins this season but pulled up on handicap debut at Haydock on Wednesday
runners_data.spotlight: Looked promising when winning maiden hurdle at Southwell (2m) in December and novice hurdle at Newcastle (2m1f, also good to soft) last month; however, pulled up on handicap debut at Haydock (2m5f, good) on Wednesday.

runners_data.name: Came From Nowhere
runners_data.note: Front-runner in tongue-tie with hat-trick form on soft ground, but 28 days since last run
runners_data.comment: May well have completed hat-trick but for final-flight mistake at Newbury; strong claims
runners_data.spotlight: Improved in this tongue-tie in the winter, winning two handicaps (2m3f, soft), and he may well have completed a hat-trick but for a final-flight mistake in a novice at Newbury (2m4f, good to soft) four weeks ago; this smooth-travelling sort could have more left in the tank; strong claims.

runners_data.name: A Perfect Day
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid handicap form but stepping up significantly in trip
runners_data.comment: Runner-up at Uttoxeter last month and winner followed up at Aintree last week; key player
runners_data.spotlight: Has done well since moving into handicaps, winning at Lingfield (2m7f, good to soft) in December and second of 14 at Uttoxeter (2m4f, soft) last month behind Wellington Arch, who followed up at Aintree last week; progressing nicely and he's a key player up 3lb for last time.

runners_data.name: Phantomofthepoints
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with course form but 54 days absent and wearing tongue-plate
runners_data.comment: Won at Warwick in February and when pulled up at Fontwell last time it was a Grade 2
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth in this last year (good to soft) and he comfortably made all at Warwick (2m5f, heavy) in February; pulled up at Fontwell 15 days later but that was a Grade 2; could make a bold bid back in a handicap.

runners_data.name: Spectacularsunrise
runners_data.note: Front-runner with patchy recent form, not seen for 48 days

runners_data.name: Sanilam
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing hood with course-winning form and recent Musselburgh success
runners_data.comment: Made it 2-2 in this hood when winning on h'cap debut at Musselburgh; clearly progressive
runners_data.spotlight: Won maiden hurdle here (2m, soft) in January and back on the scoresheet in this hood on his last two starts, most recently on handicap debut at Musselburgh (2m4f, good to soft); this progressive 6yo did it nicely last time and a 5lb rise may not stop him this afternoon.

runners_data.name: Eagles Reprieve
runners_data.note: Prominent type with excellent soft ground record and 5lb claimer reducing weight
runners_data.comment: Maiden/novice wins at Kelso; did it easily last time and has potential off opening mark
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner who got off the mark over hurdles at the fourth attempt at Kelso (2m5f, soft) in November and was back on the scoresheet in a novice there (2m5f, good to soft) four weeks ago; did it easily last time and has potential off his opening mark.

runners_data.name: Captain Butler
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who appreciates the extended trip and has solid course form
runners_data.comment: Fourth of 14 at Kelso last time and the form looks solid; could again be thereabouts
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up here (2m4f, soft) in November and suited by the step back up in trip when fourth of 14 at Kelso (2m5f, good to soft) four weeks ago, beaten just over 2l; that form looks solid; could again be thereabouts.

runners_data.name: Minella Missile
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing pull-up visor but hasn't shown winning form this season
runners_data.comment: Continues to drop down weights but hasn't been shaping as though about to take advantage
runners_data.spotlight: This season hasn't been completely devoid of spark and he continues to drop down the weights, but he hasn't been shaping as though he's about to take advantage and his losing sequence is up to 11 races.

runners_data.name: Knomorediamonds
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with 3lb claimer aboard but 60 days since last run concerning
runners_data.comment: In good form this season but suspicion he's vulnerable to stronger stayers at this trip
runners_data.spotlight: Easy win at Hexham (2m4f, good to soft) last October and he's continued to run well (soft/good to soft), finishing 11l fourth of 17 at Haydock (2m5f) in January on his last handicap start; not ruled out each-way although there's a suspicion he's vulnerable to stronger stayers at this trip.

runners_data.name: Jony R
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse improved since wearing hood with recent Listed form showing class
runners_data.comment: Improved form in this hood; contested Grade 3 last time; more needed back in a handicap
runners_data.spotlight: Improved form since this hood went on, comfortably defying a penalty in novice hurdle at Down Royal (2m1f, soft) in January before respectable efforts in 2m Listed/Grade 3 races; however, further improvement is needed back in a handicap and he has to prove his stamina.

runners_data.name: Serious Operator
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in tongue-tie but tailed off last time in competitive company
runners_data.comment: Won this in 2023 on sole previous course visit and has an each-way shout
runners_data.spotlight: 9yo who was tailed off at Kelso in February last time but that was the competitive Morebattle Hurdle over 2m; in good form over 2m4f at the end of last year, winning at Newcastle then second at Aintree; won this in 2023 on sole previous course visit and has an each-way shout back up in trip.

races.paceDynamic: The Four Sixes, Phantomofthepoints, Came From Nowhere and Spectacularsunrise will ensure a strong gallop from the outset, with all four confirmed front-runners likely to press for an early advantage. The extended 2m5½f trip on soft ground will test stamina reserves as the pace inevitably tells in the closing stages. This robust early gallop will stretch the field and create a searching test of staying power. Hold-up horses with proven stamina will be perfectly positioned to capitalise as the pace-setters weaken, making this a race that strongly favours late-closing types.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the strong early pace sets up perfectly for closers
scenarios.body: The multiple front-runners will ensure a searching gallop that plays into the hands of patient ride merchants who can pick off tiring leaders. Saracen Beau and Jony R possess the class and closing kick to capitalise when the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one pace-setter gets first run on rivals
scenarios.body: Came From Nowhere's recent hat-trick attempt suggests he has the stamina reserves to outlast his fellow front-runners. His proven soft ground form and tongue-tie equipment give him the edge in a stamina duel.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If a horse can sit just off the pace and time their run
scenarios.body: Sanilam's recent course win and hood application suggest he can track the leaders before striking late. Eagles Reprieve has the right profile to sit handy and benefit from the strong gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go too fast too early
scenarios.body: The multiple pace angles could create suicidal fractions that allow a complete outsider to pick up the pieces. Knomorediamonds has been running well in defeat and could benefit from a truly-run race.

watchPoints.text: The Four Sixes and Phantomofthepoints both show concerning recent form despite being front-runners with the highest ratings
Came From Nowhere carries top weight despite excellent recent form and may not handle the pace battle
Saracen Beau represents the strongest hold-up threat with Danny McMenamin's 70% strike-rate for trainer Nicky Richards
Multiple horses returning from lengthy absences including Spectacularsunrise (48d) and Knomorediamonds (60d) in this competitive field
Eagles Reprieve and Knomorediamonds both benefit from claiming jockeys reducing their effective weights significantly

races.name: Get Home Safe With Thistle Cabs Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Eyed
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist back from 38-day break with proven stamina but mixed recent form over fences
runners_data.comment: Tough task when pulled up at Cheltenham Festival; ran well at this meeting last year
runners_data.spotlight: His chase form has been mixed this season but he faced a tough task from out of the handicap at the Cheltenham Festival (pulled up); runner-up at Kempton (2m5f) in November on last hurdle start and he was second over fences at this meeting 12 months ago (3m); might not be a forlorn hope today.

runners_data.name: Woodland Park
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with excellent soft ground record who thrives over staying trips
runners_data.comment: Second to unexposed Skelton winner at Wetherby in February and has solid claims up 3lb
runners_data.spotlight: Admirably consistent in handicaps and finished second to an unexposed Skelton winner when upped in trip at Wetherby (3m, soft) in February, pulling clear of the third; solid claims up 3lb for last time.

runners_data.name: Whistle Stop Tour
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 55-day layoff with promising course form but recent chase disappointments
runners_data.comment: Hasn't shone over fences on last two runs but each-way claims on this season's hurdle form
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten/pulled up over fences on his last two starts but he's produced positive performances over C&D (soft) on his two hurdle runs this season, finishing placed each time; each-way claims back over hurdles.

runners_data.name: Alentejo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with French hurdle wins who showed return to form at Newbury over extended trip
runners_data.comment: Ex-French 7yo; the form of his Newbury second has worked out well; firmly in calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time French hurdle winner who was pulled up on his chase and stable debut in January but returned to form when second over hurdles at Newbury (3m, heavy) in February; that latest form has worked out well and he retains the same mark; firmly in calculations.

runners_data.name: Rocheval
runners_data.note: Front-runner seeking first win in eight starts but encouraging fourth over course and distance last time
runners_data.comment: Fairly encouraging fourth over C&D in January last time but needs to build on that today
runners_data.spotlight: 0-8 since winning his first three starts in the 2023-24 season; still only six and he was a fairly encouraging fourth of 13 over C&D in January last time, but needs to build on that run if he's to threaten today.

runners_data.name: Kent De Thaix
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent form with recent Wetherby win stepping back onto preferred soft ground
runners_data.comment: Won on stable debut at Wetherby; tougher task today but unexposed over staying trips
runners_data.spotlight: Easily won a maiden hurdle at Carlisle (2m3f, soft) in December and he tapped back into that promise to win a handicap at Wetherby (3m, good) three weeks ago on his stable debut; beat just five rivals last time but this 6yo is unexposed over staying trips and could be a contender up 4lb.

runners_data.name: I Am Max
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with inconsistent form but proven course performer stepping up in trip
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent this term but ran pretty well two starts ago, and also in this race last year
runners_data.spotlight: Inconsistent this season and down the field at Haydock a fortnight ago; however, he ran pretty well when runner-up at Doncaster two starts ago and is 2lb lower than when a close fourth of 13 in this race last year; if he's on song in a first-time tongue-tie he might not be far away.

runners_data.name: Hidden History
runners_data.note: Hold-up type below par recently but won off this mark and benefits from wind surgery
runners_data.comment: A return to form is needed but cheekpieces go on and he's in top hands; not written off
runners_data.spotlight: Below par on last three starts, most recently at Uttoxeter last month following wind surgery; however, he won off this mark on his reappearance at Aintree in November and first-time cheekpieces might give him a boost; in top hands and not written off.

runners_data.name: Draco Malfoy
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid recent form who handles soft ground well over staying trips

runners_data.name: Billy Boi Blue
runners_data.note: Prominent runner defending last year's victory but poor recent form including pulled up efforts
runners_data.comment: He's struggled on his last two starts but won this last year; betting may be interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off (fences) and pulled up (hurdles) on his last two starts; a major turnaround is necessary but he runs off the same mark as when winning this race last year; not ruled out and the betting may be interesting.

runners_data.name: Hawthorn Street
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer building on recent Catterick win with consistent soft ground form
runners_data.comment: Ran well in fourth on handicap debut at Wetherby and further improvement is possible
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner who got off the mark over hurdles at the third attempt at Catterick (3m1f, soft) in February and was beaten only 4l when fourth on last month's handicap debut at Wetherby (3m, good to soft); unexposed and further improvement is possible.

runners_data.name: Irish Champ
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with decent novice form stepping into handicap company for extended trips
runners_data.comment: Stayed on strongly over 2m4f on handicap debut and this trip could be right up his street
runners_data.spotlight: 3m point winner who showed promise in novice/maiden hurdles here earlier in the year (2m/2m3f, soft) and stayed on strongly when 13l seventh of 19 on handicap debut at Down Royal (2m4f, yielding) last month; remains lightly raced and this step up in trip could be right up his street.

runners_data.name: Don Rafael
runners_data.note: Prominent runner improving for new yard with recent 3m1f victory but untested at this level
runners_data.comment: Up in grade after narrow Hereford win but he's unexposed at this sort of distance
runners_data.spotlight: He's done well since joining this yard and was having his first crack at a staying trip when winning over 3m1f at Hereford last month; did it only narrowly and is 3lb higher in a hotter race today, but he might have more to offer over this sort of distance.

runners_data.name: Patriotik
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer well handicapped on old form but showing little recent spark over shorter trips
runners_data.comment: Well handicapped on form as recent as last March but unable to pose a threat this season
runners_data.spotlight: Very well handicapped on staying form as recent as last March and it's possible the step back up in trip will be a positive; however, unable to pose a threat across his six runs this season and has to raise his game.

runners_data.name: Society Soldier
runners_data.note: Front-runner with limited recent runs but perfect record on soft ground including recent win

runners_data.name: Just Ennemi
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from wind operation after long absence with patchy recent form
runners_data.comment: Hopes are pinned on the wind op and first-time tongue-tie prompting a transformation
runners_data.spotlight: 2-3 over hurdles in France; he's returned from a long absence this season and been well beaten in a chase and handicap hurdle; hopes are pinned on the wind op and first-time tongue-tie prompting a transformation.

runners_data.name: Shoeshine Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent course specialist with two January wins here but disappointing since February
runners_data.comment: Two C&D wins in January but this 10yo may be vulnerable back up in grade
runners_data.spotlight: Course specialist who won two in a row over C&D (heavy/soft) in January; he's better than he showed when 15l third over C&D (soft) in February and the subsequent break may have helped, but this 10yo may still be vulnerable back up in grade.

races.paceDynamic: Rocheval and Society Soldier will contest the early lead, with both having genuine front-running styles that should create an honest gallop over this extended trip. Seven horses want prominent positions (Alentejo, I Am Max, Draco Malfoy, Billy Boi Blue, Irish Champ, Don Rafael, Just Ennemi, Shoeshine Boy) creating severe traffic problems turning for home. The genuine pace and soft ground will stretch the field, creating a searching test that will expose those not staying the trip. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can avoid the early scrimmaging and pick off tired leaders in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong and the prominent brigade gets tangled up 2-3 out.
scenarios.body: The genuine gallop and soft conditions will find out non-stayers among the pace-setters, allowing patient riders to sweep past tired leaders. Hold-up specialists with proven stamina will capitalize on the honest pace scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runners steal it
scenarios.trigger: If Rocheval or Society Soldier gets an uncontested lead and slows the pace mid-race.
scenarios.body: A tactical affair would suit the pace-setters who can dictate terms and kick clear when the field is still bunched. The leader will have enough left to resist late challenges on the testing ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent tactics triumph
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses and the prominent runners avoid traffic problems.
scenarios.body: The seven prominent runners will benefit from a moderate gallop that doesn't stretch their stamina, positioning them perfectly to strike turning for home. Those tracking the pace will have first run on the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete pace collapse
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners are pulled back early creating a crawling pace.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where class and tactical positioning matter more than stamina, suiting horses with high ratings who can quicken. Fresh horses returning from breaks will have the edge in a dash to the line.

watchPoints.text: Traffic chaos likely 2-3 out with Alentejo, I Am Max, Draco Malfoy, and five others all wanting prominent positions
Society Soldier and Rocheval must be allowed to dictate the pace or the race becomes a messy tactical affair
Woodland Park and Eyed are the most reliable hold-up performers if the pace becomes genuinely strong
Several horses including Hidden History and Just Ennemi returning from wind operations need market confidence
Shoeshine Boy's course form is exceptional but his February disappointment needs explaining

races.name: Jardine Utilities Race To Repair 'Hands & Heels' Handicap Hurdle (Conditional/Amateurs') (RE Series)

runners_data.name: Kap Boy
runners_data.note: Only front runner who should get uncontested lead but faces quality field of finishers from dangerous position
runners_data.comment: Perhaps handicapped on the high side but capable of having some say after a break
runners_data.spotlight: Won a bumper for Paul Nicholls and added a 2m4f handicap at Perth in October (soft) on his first run for Olly Murphy; ran well afterwards over 2m5f, and 3m was perhaps too far when last seen three months ago; he could be handicapped on the high side but capable of having some say.

runners_data.name: Guchen
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in career-best form with same jockey partnership that delivered last two wins
runners_data.comment: Hit with a 10lb hike for latest 19l win at Newbury, but he's a 6yo firmly on the up
runners_data.spotlight: Ridden by Aamilah Aswat in his last five races; he's won the last two, though a 19l margin of victory at Newbury last time (2m4f, good to soft; first-time tongue-tie) provided the handicapper with the ammunition to hit him with a 10lb hike; he still rates a likely contender as a 6yo firmly on the up.

runners_data.name: Paso Doble
runners_data.note: Prominent type whose recent heavy ground excuse and early-season form suggests bounce-back possible
runners_data.comment: His early-season form (2m3f-2m7f) offers encouragement off this mark
runners_data.spotlight: His early-season form (2m3f-2m7f) offers encouragement off this mark; last two runs well below his best, though heavy ground was a feasible excuse the last time when a tongue-tie joined his regular cheekpieces; hard to rule out.

runners_data.name: Nice One Eric
runners_data.note: Forward-going sort who impressed in maiden win but faces significant step up in class
runners_data.comment: This 5yo may need to be on a sharp upward curve if he's to defy this initial mark
runners_data.spotlight: Had them well strung out in a 2m Southwell maiden (soft) in early March but that was a modest contest, for all that the second and third horses have won since, in low-grade races on the Flat and over hurdles; this 5yo may need to be on a sharp upward curve if he's to defy this initial mark.

runners_data.name: Summergrounds
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won this race last year and benefits from 75-day freshen-up under conditions
runners_data.comment: Last year's winner who goes well fresh, so a 75-day break is probably a good thing
runners_data.spotlight: Narrow winner of this 12 months ago when 10lb lower; has shown that he can deal with this high a mark and he goes well fresh, so a 75-day break after being below par last time is probably a good thing; respected.

runners_data.name: Balboa
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up type dropping to dangerous low weight after good effort over longer trip last time
runners_data.comment: Ran surprisingly well over 3m last time at Wincanton when all his form is over shorter
runners_data.spotlight: Without a win since 2023 but he has dropped to a dangerous mark and ran surprisingly well over 3m last time at Wincanton when all his form is over shorter; goes on soft.

runners_data.name: Travis Wheatley
runners_data.note: Transformed by first-time cheekpieces last time and retains headgear from hold-up position
runners_data.comment: In the new cheekpieces he jumped well and won unchallenged at Newcastle; up 9lb
runners_data.spotlight: The first-time cheekpieces appeared to make a huge difference at Newcastle (2m1f, good to soft) where he jumped well in front and won unchallenged by just over 5l; 9lb higher in a higher grade but he arrives here a relative unknown quantity, especially over this far.

runners_data.name: Westoftignes
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with new yard bounce already shown and wears hood for tactical control
runners_data.comment: Ready winner of a Wexford handicap on debut for these connections; a hood is added
runners_data.spotlight: Narrowly denied in a Gowran handicap (2m, heavy) before changing hands for £21,000; hit the ground running for this yard when readily taking a 2m handicap on soft at Wexford; should have no trouble staying this far and a hood goes on; he's not yet exposed and quite interesting.

runners_data.name: Rickety Gate
runners_data.note: Reliable closer carrying 5lb overweight penalty which compromises chances in competitive field
runners_data.comment: It's never ideal being 5lb out of the weights in this competitive a handicap
runners_data.spotlight: Exposed five-time winner who ran perfectly well back from an absence at Carlisle but it's never ideal being 5lb out of the weights in this competitive a handicap.

runners_data.name: Thankyouandplease
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with course form whose last run unseating mars assessment of current ability
runners_data.comment: Unseated four out last time at Wincanton and in career-best form prior to that
runners_data.spotlight: Goes on all ground; unseated four out when favourite at Wincanton last time; had been in career-best form with a win at Wincanton (1m7f) and a second at Taunton (2m3f); even more needed here, however.

races.paceDynamic: Kap Boy is the sole confirmed front runner and should get an uncontested lead with Guchen, Paso Doble and Nice One Eric settling in prominent positions but unlikely to pressure early. The mid-race tempo should be moderate over 2m4½f on soft ground, allowing the large group of hold-up horses (Summergrounds, Balboa, Travis Wheatley, Westoftignes, Rickety Gate, Thankyouandplease) to travel comfortably in behind. With only one natural leader and several strong finishers, this becomes a tactical affair where the pace may not be strong enough to expose the closers. This race shape clearly favours hold-up horses who can produce a strong finish, as Kap Boy may have too much to do alone up front against multiple talented finishers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves moderate with Kap Boy uncontested early
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows multiple closers to arrive with winning chances, creating a blanket finish where class and current form separate the finishers. Travis Wheatley and Balboa benefit most from their dangerous low weights and finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals
scenarios.trigger: If Kap Boy gets away with soft fractions and the closers leave it too late
scenarios.body: His class advantage and tactical position prove decisive when the hold-up brigade fails to mount a serious challenge until too late. Guchen's prominent position gives him the best chance to respond if Kap Boy weakens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Guchen or Nice One Eric improve the pace from halfway
scenarios.body: This creates the perfect scenario for horses that can sit handy and quicken, catching Kap Boy when he tires while staying ahead of the back-markers. The moderate early pace followed by acceleration suits their profiles perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes a crawling tactical affair throughout
scenarios.body: The race turns into a sprint finish where the freshest horse or best turn of foot wins regardless of running style. Summergrounds' fresh condition after 75 days off could prove decisive in such circumstances.

watchPoints.text: Travis Wheatley retaining cheekpieces after transformed front-running win could repeat tactics and steal race
Kap Boy getting uncontested lead through early stages may prove hard to peg back despite large field of closers
Guchen's partnership with Aamilah Aswat continuing after two wins suggests confident connections
Balboa dropping to career-low mark of 106 makes him dangerous despite lack of recent wins
Summergrounds returning after 75-day break to defend title suggests trainer timing return carefully
